at.description: Where to look. Best: {by:'block', block, expected} from read_structure_map (version='my_edit'); or a section. Omit to search the whole document (exact and whitespace/Unicode-insensitive matching only).

match_mode.description: 'safe' (default): exact first; then ignore invisible differences (line endings, Unicode form, repeated spaces, curly quotes, dashes); then, only inside a block or section `at` and for a single occurrence of 12+ characters, accept a small copy slip if exactly one place is that close. Code, URLs, link targets, HTML, math, Markdown markup, digits, identifiers and each line's indentation and list/heading marker must match exactly even here. Refuses with text_match_ambiguous / text_match_low_confidence / text_match_not_found instead of guessing. 'exact': byte-for-byte only.
match_mode.title: Match Mode

input.description:
Apply typed block/section edit operations to the caller's own open
'editing' row in place.

`operations` is the same typed union of block/section edit operations
minus `resolve_conflict` (reconciliation-only, out of scope here: this
tool always targets the row's own current body, never a shared
reconciled head).

conversation_token.description: Opaque MCP conversation token. Omit or pass 'new' to start a new dtxWiki MCP chat; echo the returned envelope value to append.
conversation_token.title: Conversation Token

expected_editing_revision.description: The editing_revision from your last create/begin/update/patch response (or read_structure_map with version='my_edit').
expected_editing_revision.title: Expected Editing Revision

idempotency_key.description: 24-hour retry key scoped to actor, workspace, and command. Generate and hold it before the first send.
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

operations.description: 1-20 edits applied atomically in one revision. Every operation is resolved against the SAME current body (not against the result of the operation before it). If any operation is refused, or any two target overlapping text, nothing is changed and error_details names the operation_index. Independent replace_text ops may be combined even without `at`. Do not mix block-addressed ops (replace_block, insert_after, insert_row, delete_block) with text/section ops in one call; replace_text with a block `at` counts as a text op. replace_block takes exactly ONE top-level block and insert_row ONE table row; insert_after takes any number of blocks. Replacing or deleting a block and inserting after it in the same call overlaps: put the extra blocks in a replace_text new_text, or send a second call with the block's new hash from data.edit_receipt. Best for changing a sentence: [{"op": "replace_text", "old_text": "<sentence copied from the block>", "new_text": "<new sentence>", "at": {"by": "block", "block": "<id from read_structure_map>", "expected": "<its hash>"}}] -- a small copy slip in old_text is then forgiven (receipt match_kind='fuzzy'). Other examples: [{"op": "replace_text", "old_text": "recieve", "new_text": "receive"}] or [{"op": "replace_block", "block": "<id>", "expected": "<its hash>", "content": "New paragraph."}].
operations.title: Operations

page_id.description: Context page UUID or stable_url: /p/<workspace_id>/<page_id> or /p/<page_id> in this workspace.
page_id.title: Page Id

input.title: PatchContextEditInput

ContextEditPayload.description: The page after an edit command, plus what that command changed.

edit_receipt.description: What this write changed: sections, line/char counts, per-operation positions, and (for a patch) the id and hash of every block whose id or hash changed. replace_block keeps the block's id; a block other edits changed keeps its id while its text stays close to the old text, otherwise it gets a new one. null on an idempotent replay.

lint_report.description: Save-time fixes and findings for the final stored body.
lint_report.title: Lint Report

ContextEditPayload.title: ContextEditPayload

DraftReviewReason.description:
One reason a write did not simply publish.

Lives here rather than beside either write surface because both use it: the
MCP result names why a draft went to review, and the REST page payload names
why a save was held from publication.
DraftReviewReason.title: DraftReviewReason

EditReceipt.description: Positions and sizes of one edit: sections, lines, characters, blocks.

changed_blocks.description: Blocks whose id or hash is new after a patch, so a follow-up block-addressed patch needs no read_structure_map round trip. Unchanged blocks keep the id and hash you already hold.
changed_blocks.title: Changed Blocks

changed_sections.description: Heading paths of the sections the edit touched (max 20).
changed_sections.title: Changed Sections

EditReceipt.title: EditReceipt

line.description: 1-indexed line of the first change in the new body.
line.title: Line

line_range.description: 1-indexed inclusive line range in the body BEFORE the patch.
line_range.title: Line Range

match_kind.description: replace_text only: how old_text was found. 'normalized' ignored whitespace/Unicode differences; 'fuzzy' forgave a small copy slip inside the addressed block or section -- check the result.
match_kind.title: Match Kind

match_policy.description: replace_text only: version of the matching rules applied.
match_policy.title: Match Policy

match_similarity.description: Only for match_kind='fuzzy': 0-1 similarity of the target.
match_similarity.title: Match Similarity

matched_sha256.description: Only for a non-exact match: sha256 of the original text that was replaced (several matches joined by NUL).
matched_sha256.title: Matched Sha256

EnvelopeWarning.description:
Structured warning attached to MCP/REST envelope responses.

Hotfix-2 renamed this model to avoid shadowing Python's builtin warning
base class. Wire shape (``code`` + ``message``) is unchanged; only the
Python class name and JSON Schema title move.

code.description: Stable warning code; must be drawn from WARNING_CODES.
code.title: Code

EnvelopeWarning.title: EnvelopeWarning

MCPErrorDetail.description:
One actionable defect in a rejected tool call.

Shaped for a caller that has to repair its own request: `field` locates the
problem, `message` states it, and `fix` says what to send instead. Never
echo the offending value here — a rejected `body_markdown` can be a
megabyte, and reflecting client input back into a response (and into the
stored trace) is both wasteful and an injection vector.
MCPErrorDetail.title: MCPErrorDetail

conversation_token.description: Opaque MCP conversation token. Echo this value on the next tool call to append to the same dtxWiki MCP chat.
conversation_token.title: Conversation Token

TextMatchCandidate.description:
Where replace_text's old_text nearly matched, by position only.

Evidence for a refused match, so the caller can re-address one block
instead of re-reading the page. It deliberately carries no text: the
candidate is page content, and echoing it would put authored text into
server guidance and the durable trace.
TextMatchCandidate.title: TextMatchCandidate
